rights: Original attributed research summaries and original Lazo synthesis. Linked third-party works retain their own rights; no full books, source articles, transcripts or private inbox messages are bundled.
limitations: 120 research entries are not 120 completed dossiers.
Read scope is explicit: selected passages, email, show notes, abstract or destination only.
These are candidate methods; software tests do not establish product judgement quality.
No full-book review is added by this pack.

cards.title: Research starts with a decision
cards.author: Erika Hall
cards.read_scope: Relevant article passages reviewed; practitioner method.
cards.locator: Opening discussion of research questions and organisational decisions.
cards.lesson: Specify what the team needs to learn before choosing interviews, surveys or another method. A question that the organisation must answer is different from a question asked directly to a participant.
cards.evidence: Original practitioner explanation; no causal outcome study assessed.
cards.limits: Useful for discovery and stakeholder alignment. It does not determine sample size or make self-reported customer intentions reliable.
cards.exercise: For Lazo's next feature, write the decision, three uncertainties and the evidence that could change the decision. Reject any interview question that cannot inform one of those uncertainties.

cards.title: Connect opportunities to an outcome
cards.author: Teresa Torres
cards.read_scope: Introductory structure reviewed; not the full archive or book.
cards.locator: Opening explanation of the opportunity solution tree.
cards.lesson: Connect a desired outcome to customer opportunities, possible solutions and assumption tests. Keep the problem space visible while considering multiple solutions.
cards.evidence: Author's framework description; broad adoption and outcome claims not independently assessed here.
cards.limits: The tree organises reasoning; it does not establish that a chosen outcome or customer need is correct. Avoid making one preferred feature look inevitable.
cards.exercise: Map one retention problem with competing explanations and two solution options per promising opportunity. Mark observations separately from assumptions.

cards.title: Make strategy hypotheses commercially explicit
cards.author: Gibson Biddle
cards.read_scope: Article introduction and framework description reviewed.
cards.locator: Introduction to delight, hard-to-copy advantage and margin.
cards.lesson: Consider customer delight, defensibility and economics together when forming product strategy hypotheses.
cards.evidence: Operator framework and historical experience; not proof that all three dimensions can be improved simultaneously.
cards.limits: Early products may temporarily prioritise learning over margin. Historical company valuations and forecasts are not reusable evidence.
cards.exercise: For each Lazo strategic bet, explain the user benefit, why it might remain distinctive, its cost to serve and the assumption most likely to invalidate it.

cards.title: Give teams strategic context
cards.author: Marty Cagan
cards.read_scope: Substantive article reviewed.
cards.locator: Responsibilities for staffing, coaching, vision, strategy and team objectives.
cards.lesson: Product leadership spans product management, design and engineering. Empowerment requires capable people and clear strategic context, alongside coaching and team design.
cards.evidence: Practitioner leadership guidance; no controlled comparison assessed.
cards.limits: Delegation should match capability and risk. Lack of context can make nominal autonomy ineffective.
cards.exercise: Replace one feature assignment with a problem brief containing the intended outcome, constraints, decision owner and escalation conditions. Ask the team to explain the choices in its own words.

cards.title: Use a shared product definition
cards.author: Ravi Mehta
cards.read_scope: Full substantive email body reviewed, 7 October 2026.
cards.locator: Product Definition email; discussion of people, agents and shared context.
cards.lesson: Keep requirements and context coherent, concise and evolving. Make clear what is included, excluded and undecided; documentation volume alone does not demonstrate clarity.
cards.evidence: Author's competency and practice guidance. Claimed reach is not evidence of business impact.
cards.limits: A document can become stale. Prototypes and conversations remain important where behaviour is difficult to express in prose.
cards.exercise: Give two collaborators the same Lazo brief independently. Compare their understanding of the problem, constraints and non-goals; fix discrepancies before adding more detail.

cards.title: Make real trade-offs discussable
cards.author: Lara Hogan
cards.read_scope: Full short article reviewed.
cards.locator: Even/over statements and review interval.
cards.lesson: Express a temporary preference between two things the team genuinely values. Tie it to a goal and revisit the trade-off rather than pretending both priorities can always win.
cards.evidence: Coaching technique; no measured causal effect assessed.
cards.limits: Some obligations are constraints, not negotiable values. A leader's statement does not resolve who has decision authority.
cards.exercise: For a contested launch, write a specific preference, its cost, the accountable decision maker and a review date. Record dissent and what evidence would reverse the choice.

cards.title: Coauthor engineering strategy with product
cards.author: Will Larson
cards.read_scope: Substantive strategy article reviewed, including the Calm example.
cards.locator: Diagnosis, policies, actions; strategy working group; Calm example.
cards.lesson: Build engineering strategy from a diagnosis, guiding policies and coherent actions. Include product partners and use concrete feedback to make decisions and resource implications understandable.
cards.evidence: Practitioner process and a self-reported company example. The article also contains illustrative scenarios that must not be mistaken for actual company results.
cards.limits: Do not copy staffing ratios or technology choices without matching organisational constraints.
cards.exercise: For Lazo, jointly write one architecture policy and the customer or business reason behind it. List the projects it changes, including an option deliberately declined.

cards.title: Bring engineering into problem solving
cards.author: Gergely Orosz
cards.read_scope: Substantive method passages reviewed.
cards.locator: Characteristics of product-minded engineers.
cards.lesson: Engineers can understand users, business goals and metrics, propose alternatives and participate in validating product choices. Their contribution extends beyond implementing a fixed specification.
cards.evidence: Operator observations; not an independently measured intervention.
cards.limits: Shared discovery does not mean every engineer needs the same role, nor that product responsibility disappears.
cards.exercise: Before committing a Lazo feature, have an engineer offer a cheaper or simpler alternative that serves the same user need. Compare user benefit, complexity and operational cost.

cards.title: Recognise coordination work
cards.author: Tanya Reilly
cards.read_scope: Opening argument and selected presentation passages reviewed.
cards.locator: Introduction to glue work and career consequences.
cards.lesson: Necessary coordination and enabling work can be poorly recognised. Its allocation and rewards require deliberate attention, particularly where it crowds out an engineer's expected development.
cards.evidence: Practitioner account; full presentation and independent outcomes not reviewed.
cards.limits: Do not conclude that PMs should absorb all coordination or that juniors should never help others.
cards.exercise: Map the last month's undocumented coordination work. Identify recurring owners, recognition gaps and work that should become a team responsibility or a simpler process.

cards.title: Measure the team's AI burden
cards.author: Camille Fournier
cards.read_scope: Article body reviewed on the author's homepage, 31 May 2026; canonical URL temporarily failed.
cards.locator: Elements of Respectful AI Use.
cards.lesson: An increase in generated output can impose review costs on colleagues. Authors should review and understand the work they pass along and make it concise enough to use.
cards.evidence: Leadership guidance based on observed frustrations; no productivity experiment assessed.
cards.limits: This is guidance for accountable collaboration, not evidence that every generated line always requires identical review.
cards.exercise: Measure Lazo task completion, correction effort and downstream reviewer time together. Do not count generated documents or code volume as success.

cards.title: Build evaluations around user tasks
cards.author: Hamel Husain
cards.read_scope: Motivation, Lucy case and initial testing sections reviewed; later sections not fully reviewed.
cards.locator: Case Study: Lucy; Types of Evaluation; Write Scoped Tests.
cards.lesson: The Rechat Lucy account describes quality plateauing as capabilities expanded. The proposed improvement loop combines task-specific tests, human/model evaluation and product experiments.
cards.evidence: First-hand implementation account; no independent business-outcome attribution assessed.
cards.limits: General model benchmarks cannot establish quality on Lazo tasks. Synthetic cases alone can miss real user failures.
cards.exercise: Create a small expert-labelled set of actual product decisions, error categories and abstention cases. Compare versions on factual support, contextual relevance and harmful omissions before testing with users.

cards.title: Extract expert procedure from actual work
cards.author: Anshumani Ruddra
cards.read_scope: Two substantive author emails reviewed: 10 September and 3 October 2026. URL is the public channel, not the email text.
cards.locator: Why product builders own AI evals; Never ask the model to invent your procedure.
cards.lesson: Use expert work, corrections and established procedures to construct reusable AI workflows. Evaluate against realistic failures rather than accepting a model's plausible procedure.
cards.evidence: Author instruction and personal examples, mixed with course promotion; scale claims not independently verified.
cards.limits: Evaluation ownership should include engineering and domain experts as appropriate; PM-only ownership is not a universal rule.
cards.exercise: Capture one experienced PM's decision, alternatives and corrections. Turn it into a candidate Lazo procedure, then test on a different case the expert has not demonstrated.

cards.title: Operations can change product outcomes
cards.author: Thejasvi Bhat — Swiggy
cards.read_scope: Implementation and results passages reviewed; 4 May 2020.
cards.locator: POP serviceability and curation changes; experimentation, rollout and results.
cards.lesson: The POP case links serviceability, curation and ordering-system changes to a better ordering experience, with experiments and staged rollout.
cards.evidence: Swiggy reports 17% more POP orders. The reviewed account does not supply enough detail to independently isolate each change's causal contribution or assess uncertainty.
cards.limits: This is a company-reported outcome, not a universal automation uplift or proof about all Swiggy practices.
cards.exercise: When Lazo users fail a workflow, inspect eligibility, data freshness and operational handoffs before redesigning the interface. Measure end-to-end completion and support cost together.

cards.title: Treat experimentation as a product
cards.author: Riteek Srivastav — Gojek
cards.read_scope: Substantive implementation passages reviewed; 27 June 2019.
cards.locator: Litmus experiment/release entities, targeting and rollout phases.
cards.lesson: Gojek describes replacing limited manual segmentation with an experimentation platform supporting targeting, traffic allocation and gradual release.
cards.evidence: Documented implementation. No quantified business uplift was established in the reviewed material.
cards.limits: Building a platform has maintenance costs; an early team may need a simpler mechanism. Release controls do not guarantee sound experiment design.
cards.exercise: Give every Lazo experiment an owner, eligible population, allocation rule, exposure record, guardrails and rollback plan before adding elaborate tooling.

cards.title: Separate a product decision from a significant metric
cards.author: Jan Overgoor — Airbnb
cards.read_scope: Experiment interpretation and example passages reviewed; 27 May 2014.
cards.locator: Sample size and stopping discussion; maximum-price filter example.
cards.lesson: The account discusses experiment pitfalls and a higher maximum-price filter shipped despite a neutral metric result because it provided user utility without an observed decline.
cards.evidence: Historical company practice and one decision account; neutrality does not prove absence of harm.
cards.limits: Do not copy historical stopping methods without statistical review. Product judgement must remain explicit about measurement limits.
cards.exercise: Predefine what an inconclusive Lazo result means. If shipping for qualitative value, record that rationale and monitor guardrails instead of relabelling the result an experimental win.

cards.title: Distinguish product love from a viable business
cards.author: Eric Migicovsky — Pebble
cards.read_scope: Summary and opening failure analysis reviewed; published 11 April 2022.
cards.locator: Why we failed; production lead-time discussion.
cards.lesson: Migicovsky attributes Pebble's failure to factors including unproven segment expansion, inventory commitments, increased operating expenses and lower margins despite a loved product.
cards.evidence: Founder retrospective. Useful failure evidence, but affected by hindsight and not an independently reconstructed causal history.
cards.limits: Do not infer that market expansion always fails or that staying in a niche guarantees survival.
cards.exercise: For a hardware or capacity-heavy Lazo customer, stress-test demand, inventory or compute commitments, margin and cash timing before recommending aggressive expansion.

cards.title: Use multiple dimensions of developer productivity
cards.author: Nicole Forsgren, Margaret-Anne Storey and coauthors
cards.read_scope: Abstract and publication metadata reviewed; full paper methods not assessed.
cards.locator: Abstract.
cards.lesson: The SPACE abstract argues that developer productivity cannot be captured by activity or a single metric.
cards.evidence: Research publication; this pass supports that framing, not a complete appraisal of the paper or a validated Lazo score.
cards.limits: Do not convert a multidimensional model into another opaque individual ranking.
cards.exercise: Pair delivery and quality measures with collaboration and reported friction. Use aggregate signals to improve the system, with qualitative context rather than individual output quotas.

cards.title: Design team interactions around flow
cards.author: Matthew Skelton and Manuel Pais — Team Topologies
cards.read_scope: Core team types, interaction modes and cautions reviewed.
cards.locator: Four fundamental topologies; three interaction modes; words of caution.
cards.lesson: Distinguish stream-aligned, enabling, specialist subsystem and platform teams. Make collaboration, service provision and facilitation explicit while considering cognitive load.
cards.evidence: Authors' organisational framework; no independent causal evaluation assessed here.
cards.limits: The source warns against reducing the approach to an org chart or isolated team labels.
cards.exercise: Map one delayed Lazo initiative's waiting time and dependencies. Propose a time-bounded change to a handoff or service contract and compare delay and rework.

cards.title: Connect growth to the product and business model
cards.author: Brian Balfour, Casey Winters, Kevin Kwok and Andrew Chen
cards.read_scope: Opening framework and organisational discussion reviewed; 31 July 2018.
cards.locator: Growth systems and functional silos.
cards.lesson: The article connects product, distribution and monetisation, using loops to reason about growth and the costs of fragmented functional goals.
cards.evidence: Practitioner framework; named coauthors form one source family, not four independent validations.
cards.limits: A loop diagram does not prove compounding, positive unit economics or durability. Funnels can still describe conversion steps.
cards.exercise: Map the proposed Lazo loop, then identify its weakest measured conversion, recurring input cost and saturation condition. Compare against a simpler acquisition model.

cards.title: Make values usable in decisions
cards.author: Bryan Cantrill — Oxide
cards.read_scope: Substantive operating document reviewed.
cards.locator: Mission, principles and values.
cards.lesson: An explicit operating document can distinguish mission, principles and values and clarify how a company expects people to make trade-offs.
cards.evidence: A first-party organisational artifact, not evidence that these values caused company success.
cards.limits: Values become useful through decisions and accountability; copying the wording does not reproduce the organisation.
cards.exercise: Write two Lazo decision examples where a proposed value has a real cost. If it never changes an action, refine it or remove it.

cards.title: Preserve expert knowledge of exceptions
cards.author: Michael Lopp
cards.read_scope: Full essay body reviewed; 20 October 2026.
cards.locator: The Insider; The Process Inflection Point.
cards.lesson: Lopp's anecdote describes how deep system knowledge helps resolve cases outside standard workflows.
cards.evidence: Personal anecdote and management interpretation. Claims about other actors' incentives are the author's interpretation, not independently verified facts.
cards.limits: A story about an expert resolver is not a reason to depend permanently on heroics or bypass controls.
cards.exercise: After the next exceptional customer failure, record the diagnosis and escalation path. Check whether another teammate can handle a similar case without the original expert.

cards.title: Record changed beliefs and genuine disagreement
cards.author: Charity Majors, interviewed by Gergely Orosz
cards.read_scope: Substantive emailed interview takeaways reviewed; 12 August 2026. Audio and full transcript not reviewed.
cards.locator: Publisher takeaways on changed AI views, validation and review.
cards.lesson: The takeaways report a shift in Majors' view of AI and an emphasis on stronger validation as generated code becomes cheaper. Her views on code review create a useful tension with other engineering guidance.
cards.evidence: Attributed interview summary and predictions, not established industry consensus or a measured result.
cards.limits: Do not transform a prediction about future verification into permission to ship unvalidated work.
cards.exercise: Keep both positions in Lazo. Ask what verification system, failure cost and reversibility would justify a different review policy; evaluate those conditions instead of voting by author popularity.

read_scope_legend.M: Substantive method or case passages reviewed; sometimes only the relevant section.
read_scope_legend.T: Publisher introduction, show notes or explicit takeaways reviewed; audio/full transcript not analysed.
read_scope_legend.T-email: Interview publisher's emailed takeaways reviewed; full interview/transcript not analysed.
read_scope_legend.E: Substantive author email reviewed; not the entire archive or independent validation.
read_scope_legend.E-part: Part of a substantive author email reviewed; not a complete article review.
read_scope_legend.A: Research abstract and metadata reviewed; full paper methods not appraised.
read_scope_legend.D: Author destination, article metadata, bio or source pointer located; no method evaluated.
read_scope_legend.P: Public preview or paid-content boundary reviewed; paid section not reviewed.
read_scope_legend.X: Source located but access blocked; article body not read.
